And what he wrote in it is dela lat'ana' DKIL Efi' before it is permissible. And Rabbi Yossi SA Dhihi wrote dela for the obituary Afi' after it is forbidden and dela lat'ana' ACP before it is forbidden. And on page 18 Rabbi Yochanan ruled 11. And Meski' there he did not rule Kuvati' except in what disagrees with the TAK on the day before it. But not for the day after. And in tractate RA page 19 of Meski', the reading is void except for Hanukkah and Purim, and the scribes differed on this point. There is Sal Dadoka on Hanukkah and Purim, it is not null. But regarding the prohibition before and after it, it is null. It is better before Hanukkah and Purim than the other good days written in the Maglat Taanit, and they are void. And so is the opinion of the rabbi in the Sha'e. Rule Afi' is void for the purpose of prohibition before it. And those who pray before Purim because of their blood are most acceptable to him. And he has confidence in the Book of Esther that the words of the fasts and their cries are written. And many other excuses, but before Hanukkah he remained in his prohibition, as well as the opinion of the BH:

machatzit-hashekel/3:ב: (2) From the Hebrew the Gemara 20 if not 20 and 25 when Purim falls on the fifth and sixth day. Dabioum V. He did not recite the Halachah on Purim and Arash, therefore he preached on the Fast of Esther 20 there. And Amash MA C. RNA Sec VI:
machatzit-hashekel/3:ג: (3) And in Hagahot Maimoniyot: even on Purim etc., as in Megillah 7a — R' Eliezer was sitting before Rav Kahana on Purim; it was evening and the rabbis did not come to the beit midrash, and Rav Kahana said: why did the rabbis not come? They said: perhaps they are busy with the Purim feast. He said: is it not possible for them to eat at night (i.e. the night of the 14th)? He said: the Master does not hold like Rava who said: a Purim feast eaten at night did not fulfill etc. — it implies that in other years their way was to come before their rabbi even on Purim; from his asking why they did not come etc. And in Sefer Avodat Yisrael he wondered: for it is explicit in Maharil the reason is because they are busy, and what he wrote that Esther does not teach is only a hint; therefore he wrote that if one has someone to trouble himself for him he must study before his rabbi — if so there is no proof from there that in other years those who were not busy came on erev Shabbat. One may say the intent of Hagahot Maimoniyot is that when he said perhaps they are busy with the feast — the intent is not eating the feast, for on that the language "busy" does not apply; also how did Rava sit before Rav Kahana, and Rav Kahana himself — also Rav Assi needed to eat a Purim feast. Although one must hold like Rav Kahana regarding the night meal per Mishnah Ahzaz, nevertheless on Rosh Hashanah Kesha there is a teaching darba dela izd — a meal does not prevent regular study before one's rabbi, and an hour or two of the day suffices for eating needs. Rather R' Eliezer said perhaps they are busy preparing feast needs and R' Eliezer has someone to trouble himself for him. Here one may say R' Eliezer said perhaps they are busy from doubt to judge them favorably. R' Eliezer is difficult either way: if you think they came yesterday on Fast of Esther before Rav Kahana — they had someone to trouble for them, and this is not an excuse that perhaps they are busy; if they did not come yesterday either, on Purim why did they not come today more — he should have wondered yesterday on Fast of Esther why they did not come. If because he holds as seems that if he made the feast at night he fulfilled — therefore yesterday he did not wonder knowing they were busy, unlike by day per his view the bother already passed — what is it that Rava said perhaps they are busy? This excuse is insufficient; rather he should have answered that Rava said a Purim feast made at night did not fulfill. Or at least he should understand there are matters within what he asked why the rabbis did not come. Or even if busy and they have no one to trouble for them — nevertheless they came before their rabbi on Fast of Esther; Purim itself they have time to prepare. What he said perhaps they are busy (and one strains that Purim then fell on Sunday; also possible they ate a little on Motzei Shabbat even though they ate third meal of Shabbat, as Magen Avraham in name of Bach siman 136 seif 1 — from all places they feast at night meal; nevertheless better on day when only 11th falls Thursday as above) — per words of Hagahot Maimoniyot on Purim they were accustomed thus when not busy, proven from Fast of Esther that even busy people came before their rabbi as above.

mechaber/1:main: Laws of Fast of Esther. Contains 3 paragraph: One is allowed to fast the day before and after Chanukah and Purim.
mechaber/2:main: We fast on the 13th of Adar. And if Purim falls on Sunday, we start the fast on Thursday. {Rama: This fast is not required, therefore you can be lenient for the time of the fast, for example: one who is pregnant, nursing, or not dangerously sick. And even if only you have pain in your eyes that is bothering you a lot - you shouldn't fast, and fast on a later day. But other people [who don't have these conditions] - they should not separate themselves from the rest of the congregation. And if Purim falls on Sunday, and the fast moves to the Thursday before, and it falls on a circumcision, you are allowed to eat for the circumcision, and the next day on Friday, those who ate should fast.}
mechaber/3:main: There are those who fast three days in remembrance of the fast of Esther.
mishnah-berurah/1:_: (a) It is permissible to fast before them and after them - as well as in the obituary of Shari and Bh, it was written that it is forbidden to fast before Hanukkah, and this is per the opinion of the Farah. And here are the practices of fasting before Hanukkah in return for Arah, and their custom should not be changed, but at the beginning it is not practiced that way, and ACP it is forbidden to break a fast on it, as well as on the Sunday after Hanukkah, even a single day it is permissible to fast on which you fast a fast, it is forbidden:
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (1) (b) An interest in the 13th of Adar - because in the days of Mordecai and Esther, on the 13th of Adar, they were forced to fight and stand up for themselves and they had to ask for mercy and beg the Omnipresent to urge them to take revenge on their enemies, and we found when they were on a day of war that they would be an intercessor, for they said that the the Master the Omnipresent would be an intercessor on the day he fought with Amalek, and surely even in the days of Mordecai, they would have an intercessor on that day, and therefore all Israel used to intercede BJ Badr and we read the Fast of Esther to remember that the Omnipresent sees and hears every person in his time of trouble when he repents and returns to the Omnipresent with all his heart as he did in those days:
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (2) (c) Fasting on the the Master's Day - but in Israel there is no one who fasts at the beginning because of the honor of the Shabbat, per the practice of saying forgiveness and supplications during Lent, and in Israel it is not possible to do so because they cannot bother to honor the Shabbat, and whoever was on the way and forgot that they fasted on the the Master's Day and ate and at night came to his house and heard that the world fasted today will fast tomorrow in Israel. Purim, if not when Purim falls on Sunday and he wrote in the Ar and above, it is a meiri lilach for the yeshiva, but for the regular study at the BH, it is not at all legal in this regard, as much as it is for the needs of a meal. turei-zahav/1:_: It is permissible to respond to them. the Omnipresent believed Dasur because of a stipulation in the Megillat Ta'anit that those days in which one is not interested in which the Sages observe a Yom Tov even before and after them is prohibited and even invalidated.
turei-zahav/2:_: And tomorrow on Friday they fast etc. It does not seem appropriate to rely on this in practice, since Beit Yosef brought in name of Maharam that the fast is moved to Thursday because one cannot postpone until Sunday which is Purim, and likewise one does not fast on erev Shabbat because of honor of Shabbat; and although halacha is established that on erev Shabbat one fasts and completes — that is only when its appointed time comes on erev Shabbat, but when postponed from its time it is not established on erev Shabbat. And as in responsum of Geonim: a communal fast is not fasted — when it is postponed; and Meiri on singular in chapter Kol Marbin: sons of Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava in Tannaita in Tash — what is Ashlomi — for this they said there is torture and complements, and they were used because of Dadoka a name whose time is fixed. What is written in PB Megillat Taanit applies to Fast of Damat and completes — we were in fast of Zabor; nevertheless Rama already wrote in siman 249 a singular Megillat Taanit will not complete, and here it must complete — it will not be fasted in Beit Din, and we will see if Fast of Esther in Beit Din is fulfilled he must complete until stars come out because it is his judgment; so it comes to mind that at his appointed time per sages for Thursday he will not be tormented for milah feast, and on Shabbat he will be tormented until night and Shabbat already entered — what if he is tormented part of Shabbat or all of it? Rather he will eat the milah feast at night as in gemara and siman 12; and here they forbade establishing Fast of Esther on Shabbat because of honor of Shabbat; above siman 249 Rama brought column through people of maaseh to fast on erev Shabbat Shabbat pleasure — their way to eat greedily when fasting; after all most of the world are weak after the fast — therefore the fast should not be established thus.
